newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil eases, pressured by futures,low demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil eases, pressured by futures,low demand.

text.p: NWE gas oil softened further on Monday, pressured by weakening benchmark IPE gas oil futures, sloppy supply and poor demand.
July IPE gas oil settled $1.0 lower ar $161.75 a tonne.
The heating oil market was extremely quiet. Premiums for refinery material were quoted at July IPE flat/+50 cents fob AR, while storage material was assessed at July IPE -25 cents/flat.
Low sulphur diesel barges were in a similar state with premiums talked around the July IPE +$5.50/+$6.50 level.

On the cargo side, EN590 continued to come under pressure. The arbitrage door for Algerian cargoes to the north appeared to have closed but a European Mediterranean player said he would sell to the north if he could not get the premiums he was looking for from local buyers.
There was even talk that U.S. players were considering putting cargoes into northern Europe.
Low sulphur premiums were talked in the region of July IPE +$5.00/+$6.00 cif NWE.

The 0.2 percent market was similarly moribund with Russian material valued at around July IPE flat/+50 cents fob ARA. German DIN was priced at around July IPE +$1.0/+$2.0 cif NWE. -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
